# Volume 3 — Chapter XXXIX Deals with Weddings

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

To Nell, existence seemed to resemble an anticlimax throughout the initial weeks following her journey back to Grey Shutters. The cheerful fellowship of Tabby’s Place was something she longed for. Over the course of the previous winter, she had harbored several splendid dreams, which now rested in the dust surrounding her. Given her current state of self-loathing, she was unable to start dreaming anew right away. Furthermore, she found out that, although solitude accompanied by dreams is magnificent, solitude lacking them possesses little appeal.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0000 }

Following their distressing farewell at the park pavilion, Cyril had not been seen by her again; nevertheless, prior to departing Portmaris, Dorothy visited her.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0001 }

“I’m terribly sorry that Cyril won't be your husband,” she said. “Having you as a sister was something I truly wanted. However, your decision is entirely correct. You would be bored to death by him. Although I love him and find him to be a dear sweet boy, he actually lacks any interest whatsoever. It seems as though he should be interesting, yet he is not.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0002 }

“Our friendship won't be ruined by this, will it, Dorothy?” had been Nell’s wistful question.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0003 }

“No, truly. You are far too wonderful to forfeit. Should I be unable to possess you as a sister, my intention is to retain you as a pal regardless. Furthermore, do not worry about Cyril. He is suffering dreadfully at present—I am forced to hear his ventings daily—yet he will recover from it. He constantly does.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0004 }

“Oh—always?” Nell asked, her tone shifting just a bit. “So before this, he has ‘got over it’?”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0005 }

“Dear me, yes,” Dorothy stated candidly. “On two prior occasions. And he babbled to me in the exact same manner on each occasion. It was not that the other women truly turned him down—they merely made public their engagements to different men. Naturally, upon meeting you, he swore to me that he had never truly experienced love until then—that those earlier relationships were nothing more than youthful infatuations. Even so, I do not believe there is any reason for you to be anxious.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0006 }

Nell chose to cast her worries aside, experiencing a blend of resentment and relief. It was true that Cyril had assured her she was his sole love, and he unquestionably thought so himself. Still, knowing it was probable she had not destroyed his existence brought her solace. Alternative goddesses existed, and Dorothy claimed that Cyril was bound to be adoring at a different altar. All the same, a few additional illusions were stripped from life, which Nell gloomily started to view as quite empty.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0007 }

On the night she got back, she stepped down from the porch gable wearing a sad expression.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0008 }

“Thirza, what occurred to the former Frost Maiden?”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0009 }

“Oh, I was aware that would make you feel terrible,” Thirza remarked. “It made me feel terrible too. Ever since I was a little girl, that tree had stood there. The severe gale we experienced in March knocked it down. At its center, it was decayed.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0010 }

“I am going to miss it so much,” Nell mourned. “Without it, the room in the porch gable feels different. Whenever I look out of its window from now on, I will always feel that something is missing. And oh, this is the first time I have ever returned to Grey Shutters without Isolde being here to greet me.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0011 }

“Isolde’s mind is occupied with other matters at the moment,” Mrs. Sowerby remarked meaningfully.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0012 }

“Well, tell me all the Brierley news,” said Nell, taking a seat on the porch steps, as the evening sunshine poured down upon her hair like a delicate golden shower.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0013 }

“Aside from what we wrote to you, news is scarce,” Mrs. Sowerby remarked. “I imagine it hasn't reached you that Simon Fletcher had his leg broken last week. His family benefits immensely from this. A hundred tasks, which they had constantly longed to accomplish but were unable to while he was around, are now being completed, the old crank.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0014 }

“His family was a frustrating one,” Thirza observed.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0015 }

“Annoying? Yes, quite! His mother was accustomed to standing in prayer-meeting, revealing every one of her kids’ flaws and requesting prayers on their behalf. Naturally, this infuriated them, making their behavior even worse.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0016 }

“Nell hasn’t heard the news regarding Odette from you yet,” Thirza pointed out.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0017 }

“Oh, Odette,” Mrs. Sowerby sniffled. “Well,” she reluctantly admitted, “Odette Pullen returned from the West—she arrived last week—and her wedding will be to a millionaire from Winnipeg. Be certain that Mrs. Gorham spread the news everywhere immediately.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0018 }

“My dear, faithful Odette—it brings me such joy,” Nell stated with warmth. “Every blessing in life ought to be hers.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0019 }

“Oh, I am not speaking ill of Odette. She is a pleasant girl. However, she does not belong to the millionaire category, and you will discover that except for his wealth, that man has little to offer, that is the truth. Mrs. Gorham states that he is an Englishman who acquired wealth in mining, yet I think he will prove to be a Yankee. He undoubtedly possesses wealth, because he recently lavished Odette with jewels. The engagement ring she received is a cluster of diamonds of such great size that it resembles a bandage on Odette’s plump hand.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0020 }

A certain sharp resentment inevitably crept into Mrs. Sowerby’s voice. Although Nell had apparently not been sought after by a single suitor, whether wealthy or destitute, Odette Pullen—that unremarkable, dull worker—had managed to secure a proposal from a man of immense fortune. Furthermore, Mrs. Gorham Pullen boasted beyond endurance.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0021 }

“What has been happening with Hugh Carrow at college?” Thirza inquired. “Upon seeing him when he returned home last week, he appeared so pale and thin that I barely recognized him.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0022 }

“During this past winter, his studies were very intense,” Nell remarked. “As you are aware, he earned High Honors in Classics along with the Cooper Prize. No one has won it in five years! Consequently, I believe he is quite exhausted. Every one of us is somewhat weary.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0023 }

“At least you possess a B.A., whereas Odette Pullen does not have one and never will,” Mrs. Sowerby remarked, expressing a sombre sense of gratification.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0024 }

A couple of nights afterward, Nell walked down to visit Odette, although she was out of town in Port Marlow—“getting sewing done,” Mrs. Gorham proudly told Nell. “Of course an Brierley dressmaker wouldn’t do for Odette under the circumstances.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0025 }

“Regarding Odette, a particularly pleasant piece of news has reached my ears,” remarked Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0026 }

“Indeed, Odette has managed quite well, despite not holding a B.A.,” stated Mrs. Gorham, lightly tossing her head. “Mr. Inglis possesses millions, and Europe is where they will travel for their honeymoon. Upon returning, a true marble mansion in Winnipeg will be their residence. A single difficulty faces Odette—her culinary skills are great, yet her husband forbids her to prepare meals. His wealth is such that he employs others for cooking. Their household will include a cook, a pair of additional maids, a coachman, and a general handyman. However, what of your situation, Nell? Despite all your time at college, I receive no news regarding a marriage for you.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0027 }

“Oh,” Nell chuckled, “an old maid is what I am destined to be. Truly, no one seems to suit me.” Her remark carried a touch of malice. She purposefully intended to make Mrs. Pullen remember that should she end up an unwed woman, a lack of at least one opportunity to marry would not be the reason. Mrs. Gorham, however, retaliated without delay.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0028 }

“Indeed, those overly selective young women usually wind up single, from what I see. And what is this news I am receiving regarding Hugh Carrow becoming betrothed to a Miss Calder? Wilfred Mott informs me that she possesses absolute beauty. Does truth lie in this?”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0029 }

“I am unsure whether his engagement to Miss Calder is a fact,” Nell answered with Spartan calm, “yet her great beauty is undoubtedly real.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0030 }

“I formerly believed that a marriage would come about between you and Hugh,” Mrs. Gorham remarked. “If you are not cautious, Nell, every one of your suitors will slip away from you.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0031 }

Nell chose against prolonging her fight with Mrs. Gorham. It was impossible to engage in swordplay with an opponent who answered a rapier’s lunges using the stroke of a battle axe.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0032 }

“Because Odette is out,” she stated, standing up in a proud manner, “I doubt I should remain any further today. I will return once she arrives back.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0033 }

“Please do,” Mrs. Gorham uttered with enthusiasm. “Odette lacks any pride whatsoever. Her intention is simply to mingle with her previous acquaintances precisely as she used to do. Seeing you will make her truly happy.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0034 }

At the end of May, the millionaire belonging to Odette came and whisked her away amidst grand magnificence. Discovering that Mr. Inglis was a full forty years old, as well as diminutive, slender, and somewhat graying, gave Mrs. Sowerby a malicious sense of satisfaction. You can be certain that Mrs. Sowerby refrained from holding back as she listed his defects.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0035 }

“A pill like him will require all of his gold for gilding, that is a fact,” Mrs. Agatha stated with gravity.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0036 }

“His appearance seems gentle and benevolent,” Nell stated faithfully, “and I have no doubt that Odette means everything to him.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0037 }

“Humph!” remarked Mrs. Agatha.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0038 }

Cressy Lindsay was wedded during the following week, with Nell traveling to Harborough so she could serve as her bridesmaid. The bride, Cressy, appeared as a delicate, ethereal fairy, while the Rev. Ez beamed with such intense joy that no person considered his looks to be plain.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0039 }

“Through the land of Evangeline, we’ll be taking a lovers’ saunter,” Cressy remarked, “and afterward, Tanner Street is where we will settle down. It is terrible, according to Mother—she believes Ez could find a church in a respectable location, at the very least. However, provided Ez is present, the Patterson slums' wilderness is going to blossom for me like the rose. Oh, Nell, my heart is aching with how happy I am.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0040 }

Nell continually felt joy when her friends were happy; nevertheless, being encircled on all sides by a joy that does not belong to oneself can feel somewhat lonely at times. Furthermore, things remained precisely identical once she returned to Brierley. On this occasion, Isolde was the one enveloped in the marvelous radiance that arrives for a woman as her first child is placed next to her. Nell observed the pale young mother with a particular reverence that had not previously been part of her emotions toward Isolde. Was it possible that this pallid woman, whose eyes held such ecstasy, was the small, rosy-cheeked Isolde with black curls whom she used to play with during bygone schooldays? It imparted to her a strange, abandoned sensation that she was somehow anchored solely to those former years, possessing no place in the present whatsoever.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0041 }

“Isn’t he completely handsome?” asked Isolde with pride.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0042 }

The small, chubby man bore a ridiculous resemblance to Gideon, possessing an identical roundness and redness. Though Nell was unable in good conscience to declare him handsome, she swore with complete honesty that he was charming, affectionate, and utterly lovely.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0043 }

“Prior to his arrival, I desired a female child, enabling me to name her NELL,” Isolde stated. “However, now that young Gideon has arrived, I would not swap him for one million girls. It was simply impossible for him to be anything other than his individual cherished self.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0044 }

“‘Every little baby is the sweetest and the best,’” Mrs. Wace gaily quoted. “If little Nell had arrived, your feelings regarding her would have been identical.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0045 }

Mrs. Wace was on a visit to Brierley, which marked her initial return there after her departure. She remained just as lively, charming, and understanding as she had always been. Her former female companions had given her a joyous and enthusiastic welcome upon her return. Although the wife of the current minister was an admirable woman, she was not quite a like-minded soul.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0046 }

“I am so eager for the time when he is big enough to speak,” Isolde sighed. “Hearing him call me ‘mother’ is my deepest desire. And oh, I am resolved that he will have a pleasant first recollection of me. My own earliest remembrance of my mother involves her striking me because of an act I had committed. I have no doubt that I merited the punishment, and my mother was invariably wonderful and holds a special place in my heart. Even so, I truly wish that my initial memory concerning her had been more agreeable.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0047 }

“My mother lives in only a single recollection of mine, which surpasses every other memory in sweetness,” Mrs. Wace stated. “Upon reaching five years of age, permission was granted for me to attend school on a single occasion alongside my two elder sisters. As the school day concluded, my sisters departed for home within separate companionships, as both assumed the other had me in their care. In reality, I had departed alongside a young girl who had been my playmate during recess. Together, we proceeded to her house located close to the school, where we commenced forming mud pies. An exceptionally wonderful time was being had by us at the moment my elder sister appeared, winded and enraged.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0048 }

"“Naughty girl,” she exclaimed, seizing my unyielding hand and pulling me behind her. “Return home immediately. Oh, you will be punished! Mother is extremely angry. You are going to receive a thorough whipping.”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0049 }

“I had not ever been beaten. My poor small heart was overwhelmed with dread and terror. Never in my existence had I been so unhappy as during that return journey. Being bad had not been my intention. Phemy Cameron had invited me to accompany her home, and I had been unaware that going was improper. Now, however, I was facing a whipping because of it. Upon our arrival home, my sister pulled me along into the kitchen, where mother was seated beside the fire as the twilight fell. My poor little legs shook to such a degree that standing was nearly impossible. And mother—mother simply gathered me into her arms, offering not a single word of scolding or severity, kissed me, and pressed me near to her heart. ‘I was so frightened you were lost, darling,’ she said tenderly. As she gazed down at me, I was able to see the love glowing in her eyes. She did not ever reprimand or criticize me for my actions—she merely instructed me that I must not ever depart again without seeking consent. She passed away shortly after that. That remains the sole recollection I possess of her. Isn’t it a beautiful one?”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0050 }

As she journeyed toward her house, traveling by the Aspen Path and Reedmere, Nell experienced a isolation deeper than any she had known before. Many moons had passed since she last traveled that route. The night was a rich, dark purple. The atmosphere hung thick with the scent of blooms—an intensity that was nearly overwhelming. From this excessive sweetness, the sated senses shrank back as if from a brimming glass. The birches lining the track, once the magical saplings of former days, had matured into large trees. All things were altered. Nell believed she would feel relieved once summer ended and her employment resumed. It might be that her existence would not appear so void at that point.
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0051 }

“‘I have put the world to the test—it displays no longer The romantic hues it once displayed,’”
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0052 }

uttered Nell with a sigh—and she felt instantly greatly reassured by how romantic it was to think that all romance had been stripped from the world!
{: #nw-v03-c39-p0053 }
